r0065.titleEn: Futur I and Futur II — the future with werden
r0065.content_md_en:
[sub] werden + infinitive; werden itself is not translated, the meaning sits in the verb at the end
### How it is built
werden is conjugated and stands in second position, the main verb moves to the end of the sentence as an infinitive.
Ich werde das Buch lesen. – I will read this book.
Wir werden im Sommer nach Berlin fahren. – In summer we will travel to Berlin.
### Conjugation of werden [collapse]
The verb is irregular, the stem changes in the 2nd and 3rd person singular.
person | Präsens | Präteritum |
ich | werde | wurde |
du | wirst | wurdest |
er/sie/es | wird | wurde |
wir | werden | wurden |
ihr | werdet | wurdet |
sie/Sie | werden | wurden |
### In everyday speech the future is usually the present
Präsens plus a time word is the normal way to talk about the future.
Ich gehe morgen zum Arzt. – Tomorrow I am going to the doctor.
💡 Futur I is kept for promises, forecasts and intentions — where it matters that the action has not happened yet.
### The same form as an assumption
With wohl, wahrscheinlich, sicher the construction reads not as a future but as a guess about the present.
Er wird wohl krank sein. – He is probably ill. This is about now, not about later.
### Futur II — "by that point already" [collapse]
It is built as werden + Partizip II + haben or sein.
Ich werde das Buch gelesen haben. – By then I will have read the book.
At B1 this meaning is rare. What does occur is the guess about the past: Er wird es vergessen haben. – He has probably forgotten it.
r0065.examplesEn:
Ich werde das Buch lesen. – I will read this book.
Wir werden im Sommer nach Berlin fahren. – In summer we will travel to Berlin.
Ich gehe morgen zum Arzt. – Tomorrow I am going to the doctor.
Er wird wohl krank sein. – He is probably ill.
Ich werde das Buch gelesen haben. – By then I will have read the book.
r0065.noteEn:
⚠ Tell them apart by what follows werden: an infinitive means the future, a Partizip II means Passiv.
Passiv is covered in r0066. On its own werden means "to become": Ich werde Arzt is present tense, not future.

r0066.content_md_en:
[sub] what matters is not who does it, but what happens to the thing
### Aktiv and Passiv
In Aktiv the subject acts by itself. In Passiv it receives the action instead.
Der Mechaniker montiert den Motor. – The mechanic assembles the engine.
Der Motor wird montiert. – The engine is being assembled.
The direct object of the Aktiv sentence (den Motor, Akkusativ) becomes the subject of the Passiv one (der Motor, Nominativ).
### Who does it — von + Dativ
Most of the time the agent is not named at all: it does not matter, otherwise Passiv would make no sense.
Der Motor wird von dem Mechaniker montiert. – The engine is assembled by the mechanic.
### Passiv exists in every tense
The tense is set by the form of werden, the voice by the Partizip II at the end.
tense | example |
Präsens | Der Motor wird montiert. |
Präteritum | Der Motor wurde montiert. |
Perfekt | Der Motor ist montiert worden. |
Futur I | Der Motor wird montiert werden. |
💡 The last line has two werden in a row: the first marks the future, the second marks Passiv.
### Perfekt: worden, not geworden
In Passiv the prefix ge- drops. The form geworden belongs only to the ordinary verb "to become".
Der Motor ist montiert worden. – The engine has been assembled.
Ich bin Arzt geworden. – I have become a doctor.
### How it comes out in English [collapse]
German Passiv normally turns into the English passive with "to be", or into an impersonal sentence.
Der Motor wird montiert. – The engine is being assembled. Or: they are assembling the engine.
English marks the passive with "to be" plus the third form, German marks it with werden plus Partizip II.
r0066.examplesEn:
Der Mechaniker montiert den Motor. – The mechanic assembles the engine.
Der Motor wird montiert. – The engine is being assembled.
Der Motor wird von dem Mechaniker montiert. – The engine is assembled by the mechanic.
Der Motor wurde montiert. – The engine was being assembled.
Der Motor ist montiert worden. – The engine has been assembled.
r0066.noteEn:
⚠ werden + Partizip II is Passiv, werden + infinitive is the future.
The future is covered in r0065, Partizip II in r0015, Perfekt in r0022.
